title: Scaffold jit-project-lead skill shell
description:
Create the `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/` skill directory with a thin `SKILL.md` orchestrator shell and a `references/` subdirectory, and register it for cross-project reachability via a symlink under `~/.claude/skills`.

## Background

jit-project-lead is a new strategic-tier skill sitting one level above `jit-execution-lead`, which already ships as a symlinked skill at `~/.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead` pointing into this repo's `.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead`. The new skill follows the same pattern: `SKILL.md` stays a thin router with detailed rules pushed into `references/` files read on demand. Mode-routing logic and mode bodies are explicitly out of scope for this shell (they arrive in follow-up work); this task establishes only the file layout, the skill's activation surface (its YAML frontmatter `description`), and the pre-flight steps that run before any tier derivation or mode dispatch.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/SKILL.md` exists, stays under 500 lines (roughly 5k tokens), and contains a pre-flight section plus routing stubs for tier derivation and mode dispatch, with no mode-routing block or mode-body content authored.
- [hard] REQ-02: `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead/references/` exists as a directory ready to hold detail-rule files, consistent with the split used by `.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead/references/`.
- [hard] REQ-03: `~/.claude/skills/jit-project-lead` is a symlink to `.claude/skills/jit-project-lead` in this repository, matching the existing per-skill symlink pattern (verifiable with `ls -la ~/.claude/skills`).
- [hard] REQ-04: The `description` field in `SKILL.md`'s frontmatter states a clear activation trigger for the skill, following the same convention as `.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/SKILL.md`.

## Notes

Skill prose follows the cc-sdd/superpowers register: terse imperative voice, explicit success criteria and safety/fallback paths, explicit stop-and-escalate conditions, red-flag lists over prose warnings, detail rules pushed to `references/`, no filler. Consult `../jit-research/cc-sdd/tools/cc-sdd/templates/agents/claude-code-skills/skills/kiro-spec-design/SKILL.md`, `../jit-research/superpowers/skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`, and `../jit-research/superpowers/skills/executing-plans/SKILL.md` as exemplars. Where the shell talks about the project's strategic or sub-strategic types, use placeholders such as "strategic tier" / "sub-strategic tier" rather than literal type names like `milestone`, `epic`, or `goal`.
